ontology.claim_ceiling: Machine-addressable projection of a candidate design; package integrity may be validated, but implementation, runtime conformance, authority, and promotion are not established.

owner_routes.label: Root runtime owner
owner_routes.scope: Graph expansion, routing cursor, edge evaluation, and command issuance.

owner_routes.label: Work unit or work adapter
owner_routes.scope: Domain status, confirmation, outcomes, and work-owned event meaning.

owner_routes.label: Work protocol boundary
owner_routes.scope: Addressed delivery semantics and message-envelope integrity.

owner_routes.label: Accepted-history boundary
owner_routes.scope: Journal acceptance disposition, append-only history, and per-run ordering evidence.

owner_routes.label: Executor or authority adapter
owner_routes.scope: Executor translation, admission, idempotent external effects, and trusted evidence injection.

owner_routes.label: Candidate architecture review
owner_routes.scope: Property definitions, relation constraints, profiles, findings, and source correspondence.

owner_routes.label: Learner projection builder
owner_routes.scope: Removable Atlas projections and their validation contracts.

owner_routes.label: Ontology promotion owner
owner_routes.scope: Any movement beyond proposal-only candidate status.

element_types.label: Architecture Element
element_types.definition: Any typed element in this local architecture-property model.

element_types.label: Work Definition
element_types.definition: Immutable, versioned outer contract that can describe a leaf or composite.

element_types.label: Leaf Work Definition
element_types.definition: Work definition whose body binds to an executor adapter.

element_types.label: Composite Work Definition
element_types.definition: Work definition whose body is a WorkGraph and whose boundary remains substitutable for a leaf definition.

element_types.label: Leaf Binding
element_types.definition: Declared binding from a leaf definition to an executor adapter without provider-specific behavior in the kernel.
element_types.formalization_note: Made explicit so the target of has-body is a resolved ontology type.

element_types.label: Work Run
element_types.definition: One invocation of one immutable WorkDefinition.

element_types.label: Attempt
element_types.definition: One execution attempt belonging to a WorkRun without changing its definition, graph, or authority basis.

element_types.label: Work Graph
element_types.definition: Typed graph composing addressed WorkNodes through EventTriggeredEdges.

element_types.label: Work Node
element_types.definition: Structural position in a WorkGraph that references one WorkDefinition.

element_types.label: Event-Triggered Edge
element_types.definition: Routing rule from one source event selector to one target invocation and input mapping.

element_types.label: Event Selector
element_types.definition: Versioned matcher over an event type and structural classification.

element_types.label: Input Mapping
element_types.definition: Declared transformation from selected source data to a target input contract.

element_types.label: Output Projection
element_types.definition: Declared mapping from selected child outputs into a composite boundary output.

element_types.label: Work Contract
element_types.definition: Input, output, command, event, authority, and limit declarations for a WorkDefinition.

element_types.label: Event Contract
element_types.definition: Declares event types, schemas, and structural classifications a work may emit.

element_types.label: Command Contract
element_types.definition: Declares addressed commands a work may receive.

element_types.label: Composition Form
element_types.definition: Declarative graph pattern compiled into EventTriggeredEdges.

element_types.label: Sequence
element_types.definition: Releases a successor from a declared predecessor event.

element_types.label: Fan-Out
element_types.definition: Releases multiple explicitly mapped branches from one declared event.

element_types.label: Fan-In
element_types.definition: Waits for a structural release condition and invokes a join work.

element_types.label: Gate
element_types.definition: Routes one decision-work label to exactly one declared outgoing edge.

element_types.label: Sidecar
element_types.definition: Attaches ordinary work to a primary under a declared lifecycle policy.

element_types.label: Bounded Repeat
element_types.definition: Repeats a graph under a decision work, positive bound, and exhaustion route.

element_types.label: Explicit Composition
element_types.definition: Direct typed WorkGraph form underlying all convenience operators.

element_types.label: Release Policy
element_types.definition: Structural readiness rule such as all, any, or bounded quorum.

element_types.label: Sidecar Lifecycle Policy
element_types.definition: Declares start, observation, termination, and output contribution behavior for a sidecar.

element_types.label: Work Message
element_types.definition: Versioned message in the common work-protocol envelope.

element_types.label: Command
element_types.definition: Addressed request that a target or authority adapter may reject.

element_types.label: Event
element_types.definition: Accepted record emitted by a work unit or trusted runtime adapter; acceptance does not imply confirmation, approval, or authority.

element_types.label: Event Classification
element_types.definition: Structural event role: progress, release, terminal, or diagnostic.

element_types.label: Work Protocol
element_types.definition: Logical command/event delivery boundary that neither decides nor executes work.

element_types.label: Journal
element_types.definition: Append-only accepted message history used for replay and audit.

element_types.label: Orchestrator Kernel
element_types.definition: Single root graph interpreter that validates, expands, observes, and issues declared commands.

element_types.label: Orchestration Cursor
element_types.definition: Rebuildable control projection of deliveries, satisfied edges, and enabled nodes.

element_types.label: Status Projection
element_types.definition: Rebuildable user or operator view over accepted child events without domain-state ownership.

element_types.label: Executor Adapter
element_types.definition: Boundary translating the work protocol to an external executor and reporting events.

element_types.label: Authority Reference
element_types.definition: Reference to accepted authority evidence required before command delivery or an external effect.

element_types.label: Domain State
element_types.definition: Work-owned meaning and lifecycle state opaque to the orchestrator.

element_types.label: Confirmation State
element_types.definition: Confirmation meaning and state owned by an individual gate or work unit.

element_types.label: Architecture Profile
element_types.definition: Named set of portable constraints evaluated over the local ontology.

element_types.label: Constraint
element_types.definition: Portable expectation evaluated by an ArchitectureProfile.
element_types.formalization_note: Made explicit so profile relation endpoints resolve independently of prose.

element_types.label: Property Constraint
element_types.definition: Constraint over one or more typed property observations.
element_types.formalization_note: Machine projection endpoint type implied by the candidate profile catalog.

element_types.label: Relation Constraint
element_types.definition: Constraint over relation presence, cardinality, direction, endpoints, cycles, or evidence.
element_types.formalization_note: Machine projection endpoint type implied by the candidate profile catalog.

element_types.label: Observation Projection
element_types.definition: Typed transformation of source, graph, journal, runtime, test, or audit evidence into observed facts.

element_types.label: Property Finding
element_types.definition: Explainable result retaining subject, expectation, observation, profile, evidence, forbidden inference, and owner route.

element_types.label: Evidence Reference
element_types.definition: Typed reference to direct evidence supporting or failing to support an observation.
element_types.formalization_note: Made explicit so supported-by has a resolved endpoint and evidence remains separate from findings.

properties.label: Work reference
properties.forbidden_inference: The same label or path means the same definition identity.

properties.label: Body kind
properties.forbidden_inference: A composite body grants nested orchestration authority.

properties.label: Event class
properties.forbidden_inference: Terminal means approved, successful, or permission for an external effect.

properties.label: Release mode
properties.forbidden_inference: Structural quorum proves quality, correctness, consensus, or independent judgment.

properties.label: Maximum rounds
properties.forbidden_inference: A finite round bound proves an agent terminates within any round.

properties.label: Sidecar finish behavior
properties.forbidden_inference: A sidecar may control the primary without an explicit edge.

properties.label: Message kind
properties.forbidden_inference: A command is an accepted event record or an event is permission for an effect.

properties.label: Delivery semantics
properties.forbidden_inference: At-least-once plus message idempotency establishes exactly-once business effects.

properties.label: Ordering scope
properties.forbidden_inference: Per-run ordering establishes global ordering across runs.

properties.label: Idempotency key
properties.forbidden_inference: Duplicate delivery is harmless without adapter or acceptance evidence.

properties.label: Reducer version
properties.forbidden_inference: A view without a reducer version is replayable or comparable.

properties.label: Projection freshness
properties.forbidden_inference: A displayed state is current when freshness lineage is absent.

properties.label: Authority effect
properties.forbidden_inference: Ontology membership grants authority or approval.

properties.label: Authoritative state class
properties.forbidden_inference: One owner class silently owns or reinterprets another state class.

properties.label: Evidence stage
properties.forbidden_inference: Earlier-stage evidence proves a later-stage architecture property.

relations.label: Specializes
relations.meaning: Local subtype relation; transitive only within this type hierarchy.

relations.label: Has contract
relations.meaning: Makes the uniform outer Work contract explicit for both leaf and composite definitions.

relations.label: Has body
relations.meaning: Selects exactly one composite graph or leaf binding.

relations.label: Instantiates
relations.meaning: Binds a run to one immutable definition.

relations.label: Has attempt
relations.meaning: Associates attempts without changing WorkRun identity.

relations.label: Contains node
relations.meaning: Gives a WorkNode structural membership in one graph.

relations.label: Contains edge
relations.meaning: Gives an EventTriggeredEdge structural membership in one graph.

relations.label: References work
relations.cycle_policy: graph cycles governed by bounded-cycle constraints
relations.meaning: Selects the reusable WorkDefinition at a structural graph position.

relations.label: From node
relations.meaning: Declares the edge source node.

relations.label: To node
relations.meaning: Declares the edge target node.

relations.label: Selects event
relations.meaning: Names the declared event trigger for an edge.

relations.label: Maps input with
relations.meaning: Names the target-input mapping for an edge.

relations.label: Projects output with
relations.meaning: Declares the composite boundary-output projection.

relations.label: Compiles to
relations.meaning: Desugars convenience syntax into the primitive WorkGraph without proving execution.

relations.label: Uses release policy
relations.meaning: Declares fan-in structural readiness.

relations.label: Uses lifecycle policy
relations.meaning: Declares sidecar lifecycle coupling.

relations.label: Bound to
relations.meaning: Selects the external executor boundary for a leaf binding.

relations.label: Receives
relations.meaning: Records an addressed request received by a WorkRun.

relations.label: Emits
relations.meaning: Attributes an Event to its producing run or trusted adapter.

relations.label: Delivered by
relations.meaning: Identifies the logical protocol boundary used for delivery.

relations.label: Recorded by
relations.meaning: Records event persistence without creating confirmation or domain state.

relations.label: Expands
relations.meaning: Expands nested definitions into one addressed root plan.

relations.label: Issues
relations.meaning: Issues a declared addressed command without deciding the work's domain outcome.

relations.label: Derived from
relations.meaning: Makes projection lineage explicit and rebuildable.

relations.label: Observes
relations.meaning: Exposes an accepted event record without owning its domain meaning.

relations.label: Requires authority
relations.meaning: Names required authority evidence without deciding or granting it.

relations.label: Owned by
relations.meaning: Places domain-state semantics outside the OrchestratorKernel.

relations.label: Evaluates
relations.meaning: Selects explicit constraints for an ArchitectureProfile.

relations.label: Supported by
relations.meaning: Grounds an observed finding in evidence that remains a separate record.

shields.forbidden_inference: Composite definition or graph containment implies an orchestrator-to-orchestrator invocation edge.
Parentage, containment, or node path transmits tools, context, budget, evidence, confirmation, or authority.
Observing an event or maintaining a cursor makes the OrchestratorKernel owner of DomainState or ConfirmationState.
Delivering or recording a message means the WorkProtocol or Journal authorized, decided, confirmed, or executed it.
A terminal classification means success, approval, acceptance, truth, or permission for an effect.
A StatusProjection manufactures confirmation, authority, freshness, or child domain facts.
quorum(n) means independent evidence, correctness, quality, or consensus.
Schema-valid input, output, command, or event is semantically correct or fit for purpose.
A stable message key proves the external effect is idempotent or occurred exactly once.
Inclusion in this package promotes a term, constraint, source, architecture claim, or owner decision.

constraint_operators.label: All subjects
constraint_operators.portable_semantics: Every instance of the selected subject types must satisfy the nested requirement.

constraint_operators.label: Exactly one
constraint_operators.portable_semantics: Exactly one matching property or relation value must exist.

constraint_operators.label: Complete edge
constraint_operators.portable_semantics: Every selected edge must have one source, target, selector, and input mapping.

constraint_operators.label: Unique match
constraint_operators.portable_semantics: A routing label or selector resolves to exactly one admitted target.

constraint_operators.label: Positive bound
constraint_operators.portable_semantics: Every selected cycle has a positive finite bound and an exhaustion route.

constraint_operators.label: Requires evidence
constraint_operators.portable_semantics: A claim is supportable only when evidence at or above the named stage exists.

constraint_operators.label: Deterministic equivalence
constraint_operators.portable_semantics: Equal canonical inputs under the same version produce byte-identical canonical outputs.

constraint_operators.label: Reject unknown
constraint_operators.portable_semantics: Unknown kinds, versions, operators, schemas, or capabilities are rejected rather than defaulted.

constraints.label: Uniform outer contract
constraints.expectation: Every leaf and composite definition has one versioned outer WorkContract and exactly one body matching body-kind.

constraints.label: Shallow runtime authority
constraints.expectation: Nested composites expand into one root plan and no graph node invokes another OrchestratorKernel.

constraints.label: Complete routing edge
constraints.expectation: Every routing edge names one source, target, event selector, and input mapping.

constraints.label: Single-valued gate route
constraints.expectation: Every admitted gate route label resolves to exactly one explicit outgoing edge; zero or multiple matches fail closed.

constraints.label: Explicit fan-in policy
constraints.expectation: Every FanIn declares one release policy and a canonical input ordering.

constraints.label: Bounded cycles
constraints.expectation: Every cyclic component names a decision work, positive bound, exhaustion edge, and no-next-attempt result.

constraints.label: Idempotent acceptance
constraints.expectation: Commands and accepted events use stable keys; identical duplicates converge and divergent same-key bytes quarantine.

constraints.label: Non-authoritative projection
constraints.expectation: Every projection retains reducer, freshness, and event lineage and cannot emit authority or child domain facts.

constraints.label: No parent inheritance
constraints.expectation: Every child materialization names its tools, context, budget, evidence, and authority explicitly.

constraints.label: Effect authority boundary
constraints.expectation: Every external-effect command crosses an adapter with an accepted authority reference; reference presence, adapter admission, and effect occurrence remain separate.

constraints.label: Deterministic cursor replay
constraints.expectation: Identical canonical ordered history and reducer version rebuild byte-identical cursor state.

constraints.label: Fail-closed extensibility
constraints.expectation: Unknown operator, command, event, schema version, or capability is rejected rather than guessed or defaulted.

profiles.label: Core candidate profile
profiles.claim_ceiling: May report per-constraint findings only at the stage actually observed; no aggregate conformance pass follows from missing later-stage evidence.

profiles.label: Definition and graph profile
profiles.claim_ceiling: May establish candidate definition and graph consistency for observed fixtures; cannot establish delivery, replay, adapter, authority, or runtime conformance.

profiles.label: Runtime evidence profile
profiles.claim_ceiling: Requires implementation, runtime traces, tests, and telemetry that are absent from this package.

finding_contract.absence_rule: Absent evidence yields unsupported or indeterminate, never pass.

premises.claim: Leaf and composite definitions share one outer Work contract.
premises.falsification: A required composition cannot expose the same input, output, command, and event boundary without leaking scheduler semantics.

premises.claim: One root OrchestratorKernel can expand every nested composite in a bounded run.
premises.falsification: A supported bounded graph requires independently authoritative nested schedulers to preserve correctness or ownership.

premises.claim: Declared commands and events are sufficient for the thin orchestration kernel.
premises.falsification: A bounded workflow requires the kernel to own domain judgment not expressible as work, policy, adapter, or declared event-triggered relation.

premises.claim: Individual work units or adapters own confirmation and domain status.
premises.falsification: A required routing guarantee cannot be implemented unless the kernel becomes authoritative for the work's domain state.

premises.claim: At-least-once delivery plus mandatory idempotent acceptance is the appropriate baseline.
premises.falsification: Concrete process and host boundaries require stronger or different guarantees that cannot remain adapter-owned.

premises.claim: Finite or explicitly bounded event-triggered WorkGraphs cover almost any bounded pipeline in the stated scope.
premises.falsification: A bounded counterexample needs a primitive outside typed work nodes, declared command/event triggers, explicit mappings, and bounded cycles.

residue.question: May a WorkDefinition extend its graph dynamically, and what confirmation binds the changed topology?
residue.ontology_impact: Graph version and authority relations remain incomplete.

residue.ontology_impact: The composition-form catalog may need extension.

residue.question: Should quorum(n) remain structural, or must every quorum be decided by a gate work unit?
residue.ontology_impact: The release-policy semantic boundary remains open.

residue.question: How are schema and reducer migrations replayed without reinterpreting history?
residue.ontology_impact: Version and replay relations remain incomplete.

residue.question: What is the minimal AuthorityReference the kernel may verify without owning authorization policy?
Which counterexample suite is sufficient for the bounded any-pipeline claim?
residue.ontology_impact: Bounded expressiveness remains unsupported beyond included examples.

residue.question: Does long-lived streaming work fit the Work boundary or require a distinct subscription construct?
residue.ontology_impact: Closure of the uniform Work contract remains unproven.

residue.question: Which owner may promote the design and ontology beyond proposal-only?
residue.ontology_impact: The ontology remains proposal-only and the promotion route is blocked.

residue.question: Is EventClassification metadata on an EventContract, an independent controlled vocabulary, or both?
residue.ontology_impact: The representation remains an independent local type with property use; no canonical form is selected.

residue.question: Must InputMapping be pure and deterministic, or may it invoke a mapping WorkDefinition?
residue.ontology_impact: Mapping execution and evidence rules remain incomplete.

residue.question: Is an ExecutorAdapter work-owned or an independently governed runtime boundary?
residue.ontology_impact: Adapter ownership remains external and unresolved by this ontology.

residue.ontology_impact: Only rwo:r.specializes is transitive; every other relation remains non-transitive pending review.

residue.question: Should the frozen conceptual ONTOLOGY.md retain document-level veracity and conviction fields even though local conventions omit them for conceptual nodes?
residue.ontology_impact: The source remains byte-pinned for accepted research; a later owner-reviewed source refresh must resolve the frontmatter convention mismatch without rewriting history.

residue.question: When should DESIGN.md stop saying the candidate recursive-work ontology is not yet created?

residue.question: How should the accepted view research be refreshed now that a candidate machine graph and hand-authored HTML canvas exist but no projection compiler, accessibility evaluation, or comprehension study exists?
residue.ontology_impact: The research remains correct as a frozen snapshot; current state must distinguish a locally browser-tested removable HTML candidate from a generated projection, accessible interface, comprehended explanation, or runtime view.
